*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health
emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order
N-29-20 (https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting of August
10, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1. Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically
  for consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City
  Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at
  aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to
  consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and in
  the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence should
  indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to the close
  of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office
  of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any question.

  2. In Person: The Library Lecture Hall (located adjacent to the Main Library) will be open to provide
  members of the public with an opportunity to address the Legislative Body on Open Session Items.

  3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider for
  details.

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  August 10, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  August 10, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
  hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts/Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority
  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agendas.

  There was no response.
142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Dotson that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  August 5, 2021, in the amount of $3,153,850.28 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Dotson that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on March 29, 2021
  (Special) and April 6, 2021, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  AGREEMENT NO. 21-218 APPROVED – CSG CONSULTANTS, INC;
  AGREEMENT NO. 21-219 APPROVED – NABIH YOUSSEF ASSOCIATES
  STRUCTURAL ENGINEERS. Staff report dated August 10, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of three-year professional services agreements (with the option
  to extend for two additional years, in one-year increments) to provide building plan check
  services for the Inglewood Basketball and Entertainment Center (IBEC).
   August 10, 2021

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 21-218 with CSG
  Consultants, Inc., in an amount not to exceed $1,669,339; and 2) Approve Agreement
  No. 21-219 with Nabih Youssef Associates Structural Engineers in an amount not to
  exceed $506,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  RESOLUTION NO. 21-132 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL 2020-2021
  BUDGET TO HIRE CONSULTANTS FOR PLAN CHECK SERVICES FOR THE
  INGLEWOOD BASKETBALL AND ENTERTAINMENT CENTER (IBEC)
  PROJECT. Staff report dated August 10, 2021, was presented recommending adoption
  of a resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Budget in the amount of $3,000,000,
  to hire consultants for Plan Check services for the Inglewood Basketball and
  Entertainment Center (IBEC) project, and Inspection services for other City projects.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that Resolution No. 21-132 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2020-21 ANNUAL
  BUDGET TO HIRE CONSULTANTS FOR PLAN CHECK SERVICES:
  1) FOR THE INGLEWOOD BASKETBALL AND ENTERTAINMENT
  CENTER PROJECT AND 2) AND INSPECTION SERVICES FOR
  OTHER CITY PROJECTS

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  LIBRARY PROGRAM GRANT ACCEPTED – CALIFORNIA STATE LIBRARY;
  RESOLUTION NO. 21-133 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-
  2021 BUDGET. Staff report dated August 10, 2021, was presented recommending
  approval to accept the Lunch at the Library Program Grant funding from the California
  State Library.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve acceptance of the grant funding in the amount
  of $24,800; and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 21-133 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2020-2021
  ANNUAL BUDGET TO ACCEPT THE LUNCH AT THE LIBRARY
  PROGRAM GRANT FUNDING FROM THE CALIFORNIA STATE
  LIBRARY

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  FIRST AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 19-025 APPROVED – LIFTECH
  ELEVATOR SERVICES, INC. Staff report dated August 10, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of the first amendment to Agreement No. 19-025 with Liftech
  Elevator Services, Inc. (Liftech), extending the contract for an additional year (to expire
  on October 23, 2022) for elevator maintenance and repair services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby approve amendment to Agreement No. 19-025 in an
  additional amount not to exceed $110,121 (includes a ten (10%) contingency in an
  amount not to exceed $10,011 for emergency repair service). The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:

  2
   August 10, 2021

  Ayes:  Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

 183  RESOLUTION NO. 21-134 ADOPTED – CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION
  RECYCLING PROGRAM, AMENDING THE CITY’S 2020-2021 ANNUAL
  BUDGET. Staff report dated August 10, 2021, was presented recommending adoption
  of a resolution retaining certain Construction and Demolition Recycling Program
  performance security deposits pursuant to Inglewood Municipal Code 7-71, et seq., and
  amending the City’s 2020-2021 Annual Budget.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that Resolution No. 21-134 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA  RETAINING  CERTAIN
  CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION RECYCLING PROGRAM
  PERFORMANCE  SECURITY  DEPOSITS  PURSUANT  TO
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE 7-71, ET SEQ. AND AMENDING
  THE CITY’S 2020-2021 ANNUAL BUDGET

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 21-220 APPROVED – KOA
  CORPORATION. Staff report dated August 10, 2021, was presented recommending
  award of a professional services contract and approval of an agreement with KOA
  Corporation to provide construction management services for the Centinela Street
  Improvement Project, per Request for Proposals No. RFP-0166.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby award a professional services contract and approve
  Agreement No. 21-220 in an amount not to exceed $460,636 (includes a ten percent
  (10%) contingency in an amount not to exceed $41,876). The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

131.8  REALLOCATION OF FUNDS APPROVED – CITY OF INGLEWOOD RENT
  RELIEF PROGRAM; RESOLUTION NO. 21-142 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 BUDGET. Staff report dated August 10, 2021, was
  presented recommending approval of the reallocation of funds for staffing and other
  administrative costs to administer the City of Inglewood Rent Relief Program.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve reallocation of funds; and 2) Adopt
  Resolution No. 21-142 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2020-2021 BUDGET TO REALLOCATE CARES ACT CDBG-CV
  FUNDING  TO  PAY  FOR  SALARIIES AND  OTHER
  ADMINISTRATIVE COSTS TO ADMINISTER THE COVID-19
  INGLEWOOD RENT RELIEF PROGRAM

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  ORDINANCE NO. 21-12 ADOPTED – ZONING CODE AMENDMENT 2020-001
  TO CHAPTER 12 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE. Staff report dated
  August 10, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of Ordinance No. 21-12

  3
 August 10, 2021

  approving Zoning Code Amendment 2020-001 (ZCA-2020-001) to Chapter 12 (Planning
  and Zoning) of the Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC) to modify regulations for off-hour
  parking for major event patrons and tailgating Citywide.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that Ordinance No. 21-12 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, TO APPROVE ZONING CODE
  AMENDMENT 2020-001 (ZCA-2020-001) TO AMEND ARTICLES
  1,1.1,10 AND 19 OF CHAPTER 12 (PLANNING AND ZONING) OF
  THE  INGLEWOOD  MUNICIPAL  CODE  TO  MODIFY
  REGULATIONS FOR OFF-HOUR PARKING FOR MAJOR EVENT
  PATRONS AND TAILGATING CITYWIDE

  which was introduced at the meeting held on August 3, 2021, be adopted. The motion
  was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Speaker (Name Unknown), commented on Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item Nos. 2,
  Approval of the Minutes of the Meetings held on March 29, 2021 (Special), and April 6,
  2021, O-1, Adoption of Ordinance No. 21-12 approving Zoning Code Amendment 2020-
  001 to Chapter 12 of Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC). She also commented on time
  limits allowed to speak on Agenda Items.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the memory of Doris Sweeney, Richard Farris, Jr., and Kathy Thompson at
  the hour of 2:16 p.m.

  Approved this 12th day of October, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
